items.title: Theoretical Prediction of Superconductivity and Nontrivial Band Topology in Rock-Salt Transition-Metal Hydrides MH (M = Mo, W, Ru, Rh, Y)
authors: Yan-Li Zhang, 艳丽 张, Hao Ding, 豪 丁, Han Wang, 菡 王, Ya-Ping Li, 牙平 李, Jin-Han Tan, 锦函 谭, Na Jiao, 娜 焦, Rui Wang, 锐 王, Hong-Yan Lu and 洪艳 路
items.summary: Transition-metal hydrides have recently emerged as a promising platform for exploring the interplay between superconductivity and nontrivial band topology. Here, using first-principles calculations, we predict a family of rock-salt transition-metal monohydrides MH (M = Mo, W, Ru, Rh, Y) that are stable at ambient pressure. Our calculations show that these compounds exhibit phonon-mediated superconductivity, with estimated superconducting transition temperatures of 14.6 K, 14.5 K, 5.3 K, 7.9 K, and 4.5 K for MoH, WH, RuH, RhH, and YH, respectively. For MoH and WH, the electron–phonon coupling is mainly contributed by the softened low-frequency phonon modes associated with transition-metal vibrations, which couple strongly to the doubly degenerate d-orbitals ( and ) near the Fermi level. In addition, spin–orbit coupling opens nontrivial band gaps near the Fermi level, as confirmed by topological invariants and topologically protected surface states. These results identify rock-salt transition-metal monohydrides as promising ambient-pressure platforms for investigating the coexistence of superconductivity and nontrivial band topology.

items.title: Photoexcited Polaron Dynamics in Rutile TiO2 from First-Principles On-the-Fly Surface Hopping
authors: Chang Gao, 畅 高, Qijing Zheng, 奇靖 郑, Jin Zhao and 瑾 赵
items.summary: Photoinduced polaron dynamics challenges the classical path approximation (CPA), which prescribes nuclear motion on a single potential-energy surface (PES). To overcome this limitation, we use ΔSCF-based on-the-fly surface hopping involving both ground- and excited-state PESs to study photoexcited polaron dynamics in rutile TiO2. The simulations capture electron and hole polaron formation, migration, recombination, and subsequent ultrafast lattice relaxation. The electron–hole recombination lifetime increases by approximately two orders of magnitude relative to CPA-nonadiabatic molecular dynamics, from 38 ps to 6.3 ns. This increase arises from reduced nonadiabatic coupling: excitation-induced electron redistribution substantially changes the orbitals relative to the ground state at the same nuclear geometry. These results highlight the importance of orbitals associated with both PESs and lattice feedback in electron–hole recombination. The approach provides a tool for investigating excited-state dynamics in solids where the CPA breaks down.

items.title: Nonreciprocal Relaxation Acceleration
authors: Xingyu Zhang, 星宇 张, Yihan Ma, 艺函 马, Yue Liu, 越 刘, Niaz Ali Khan, Chenlong Huang, 晨龙 黄, Yuguo Su, 玉国 苏, JunYan Luo, 钧炎 骆, Dahai He and 达海 贺
items.summary: Driven by recent discoveries regarding the quantum Mpemba effect, the anomalous relaxation dynamics of open quantum systems have garnered significant attention. While expediting thermalization to equilibrium has been extensively studied, dynamically accelerating the convergence toward nonequilibrium steady states remains a formidable challenge. In this Letter, we find that a transiently engineered nonreciprocal dissipative channel can provide a shortcut that accelerates relaxation to the target reciprocal nonequilibrium steady state. Using a two-mode interacting bosonic model, we demonstrate that the temporal activation of a nonreciprocal channel efficiently suppresses prolonged inter-mode energy oscillations, enforcing a rapid, unidirectional thermal dump into the environment. Counterintuitively, under symmetric local dissipation, both nonreciprocal directions exhibit relaxation speedup with identical asymptotic spectral decay rates. Our results establish a route to accelerated nonequilibrium steady-state preparation in the studied bosonic model, with a covariance-based sufficient condition that extends to a multimode chain.

items.title: Kelvin-Temperature Ultracold Electron Beam
authors: Haoyu Huang, 浩宇 黄, Haibo Wang, 海波 王, Jianing Sun, 佳宁 孙, Enliang Wang, 恩亮 王, Xu Shan, 旭 单, Chunkai Xu, 春凯 徐, Xiangjun Chen and 向军 陈
items.summary: We report an ultracold electron beam with Kelvin-level transverse temperature generated from a cold atom electron source by two-color near-threshold photoionization of 87Rb atoms in a magneto-optical trap. A novel self-referenced scheme was employed to precisely determine its transverse temperature. In this scheme, a 3 × 3 beam array was generated to provide an in situ reference, allowing the transfer-matrix element to be determined directly from the measured grid pattern. The transverse momentum spread of the central beam at the source plane is then retrieved, yielding a transverse temperature of T = 2.0 ± 1.0 K, with the corresponding intrinsic coherence length of Lc = 21.1 ± 5.0 nm and a relative coherence length of C = (1.3 ± 0.4) × 10−3. The new scheme significantly suppresses the influence of residual magnetic fields, electric field inhomogeneities, and electron-optical aberrations. A non-monotonic dependence of the transverse temperature on excess energy was observed and was qualitatively explained by the simulation using a polarization-dependent single-atom Coulomb–Stark trajectory model.

items.title: Multiple Moiré Polarization Textures in Twisted Trilayers
authors: Haoshen Ye, Ying Zhou and Shuai Dong
items.summary: Twisted van der Waals layers exhibit nontrivial polarization textures from moiré-modulated stacking and the inherited sliding ferroelectricity. However, in any twisted bilayer, the topology of the polarization texture is essentially fixed due to the inherent twist-stacking landscape for a given material. Here, this constraint is overcome in certain twisted trilayers, where the relative moiré phase emerges as an additional structural degree of freedom. Using CrI3 and BN as representative sliding ferroelectrics with distinct symmetries, we clarify how the relative moiré phases reshape the trilayer stacking landscapes and tune the net polarization texture via layer sliding. The multiple moiré polarization textures can be attributed to the interference of original moiré patterns of the two bilayer subsystems.

items.title: Lattice in Line: Optimized DMRG ordering for complex lattice geometries
items.summary: The density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) is a one-dimensional tensor-network technique, but it is not limited to one-dimensional systems: it can be applied to periodic 2D and 3D clusters and molecules, provided their sites are first enumerated along a line; a step one may call ``lattice compilation''. This paper discusses three proxy loss functions for finding this optimal enumeration: the graph bandwidth $B$ (maximum interaction range), the cutwidth $C$ (maximum number of bonds crossing a cut), and the average interaction range $R$. Constructing the Hamiltonian MPO (matrix-product operator) for a large set of clusters that are of interest in frustrated magnetism, I find that $C$ determines the peak SU(2) Heisenberg MPO bond dimension and $R$ the average one. Targeting $(C,R)$ lexicographically yields the best energies. Targeting $B$ indirectly reduces $C$, but not as efficiently as targeting $C$ directly. Otherwise, the value of $B$ itself is largely irrelevant in the sense that good DMRG energies can have large $B$. To perform the optimization, classic heuristics (e.g.\ reverse Cuthill--McKee) prove unreliable even for small clusters, and I find that a QUBO formulation improves them only marginally. Instead I propose a staged optimization built on Boolean satisfiability (SAT) and constraint-programming (CP) solvers, CP-SAT of Google's OR-Tools (a hybrid of CP propagation and SAT clause learning) and the SAT solvers CaDiCaL and Glucose. This approach yields significantly better orderings together with rigorous bounds. The corresponding \textit{Lattice in Line} code is available at https://github.com/spinflip/lattice_in_line and was designed with extensive use of the Fable 5 large language model.

items.title: Design of Chalcopyrite-Inspired Tellurides for Solar Cells: A First-Principles and Coupled FDTD-CHARGE Device Study
items.summary: The defect-chalcopyrite tellurides XGa$_2$Te$_4$ (X = Cd, Zn) are evaluated as photovoltaic absorbers by combining first-principles calculations with coupled optical and electrical device simulations. Density functional theory (PBEsol) yields tetragonal $I\bar{4}$ structures with negative formation energies and phonon spectra free of imaginary modes. Both compounds have direct band gaps at $Γ$ of 1.046 and 1.032 eV (PBEsol) and 2.21 and 1.895 eV (HSE06), with absorption coefficients above $10^5$ cm$^{-1}$ in the visible. Wannier-Mott estimates give exciton binding energies of 18.85 and 26.81 meV, comparable to $k_BT$ at 300 K, and Bohr radii of 3.43 and 2.30 nm. Constant-relaxation-time Boltzmann transport gives Seebeck coefficients up to ~255 $μ$V K$^{-1}$ near 350-400 K. Mulliken-electronegativity estimates place both band edges outside the water redox potentials at pH 0, with hydrogen-evolution driving forces of 0.83 and 0.60 eV but oxygen-evolution margins of only 0.16 and 0.07 eV. Finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) optical simulations coupled to drift-diffusion (CHARGE) electrical simulations of FTO/IGZO/XGa$_2$Te$_4$/CuAlO$_2$/Pt cells reveal a small conduction-band spike at the front junction (+0.15 and +0.33 eV), reflection losses governed by interference in the front oxide stack, electron collection confined to ~0.5 $μ$m from the junction, and a fill-factor loss in the CdGa$_2$Te$_4$ device caused by the CuAlO$_2$ hole contact. Because the imported optical constants retain the PBEsol absorption edge, the simulated photocurrents exceed the detailed-balance limit; absolute efficiencies are therefore treated as upper bounds, whereas the identified loss mechanisms and design trends are robust. These results identify CdGa$_2$Te$_4$ and ZnGa$_2$Te$_4$ as candidate thin-film absorbers and define the contact engineering required to exploit them.

items.title: Activity-induced response amplification and instability near jamming in a Wishart--Ginibre model
items.summary: We study the linear mechanical response of a disordered contact network using an additive Wishart--Ginibre model: a passive Wishart operator is perturbed by an independent real Ginibre coupling of strength \(α_0\). The observable is the mean-square static displacement response per degree of freedom, normalized by the variance of the applied isotropic forces, rather than a shear compliance. In the large-matrix limit, the Hermitized Dyson equation gives \(J=(1-q)^{-3}/[1-(α_0/α_c)^2]\) on the stable side, where \(q<1\) is the Wishart aspect ratio and \(α_c=(1-q)^{3/2}\). Thus the random coupling amplifies the response up to the onset of linear instability. At the unshifted isostatic point \(q=1\), the limiting spectrum enters the right half-plane for every nonzero \(α_0\), so there is no stable isostatic susceptibility at nonzero activity. Direct matrix calculations show response amplification away from the threshold and a broadened stability crossover at finite size. Near marginality, a single singular value often carries much of the inverse trace, including in unstable realizations for which that trace is not a steady response.

items.title: Photocatalytic Water Splitting in GeC/ReS$_2$ van der Waals Heterostructures
items.summary: Photocatalytic water splitting is considered as one of the most promising approaches for the green hydrogen production. But the rapid recombination of photogenerated electron-hole pairs severely inhibits its photocatalytic efficiency. Construction of van der Waals heterostructures is a good way to suppress this recombination. However, in staggered band heterostructures, the charge transfer could occur either through the type-II or the direct Z-scheme mechanism. Therefore it is very important to identify which mechanism is dominant. In the present work, we systematically study the GeC/ReS$_2$ heterostructure using first-principles density functional theory (DFT). The system exhibits good thermodynamic, dynamic and thermal stability and an indirect band gap of 1.38 eV which greatly enhances the visible-light absorption. We find that the direct Z-scheme mechanism is the dominant interfacial charge transfer by analysing band alignment and Gibbs free energy pathways. The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) can be driven spontaneously in the pH range $4 \le \text{pH} \le 14$ under light irradiation for both type-II and Z-scheme pathways but the energy barrier is much lower for the Z-scheme mechanism. Moreover, the type-II mechanism is not suitable for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), but the Z-scheme mechanism can promote HER well in the entire pH range ($0 \le \text{pH} \le 14$). Remarkably, the strain-free (pristine) condition exhibits a solar-to-hydrogen (STH) efficiency of 41.40\%, well above the 10\% threshold for commercial viability. The STH efficiency is further enhanced to 60.68\% under a tensile strain of +6\%. To summarise, the Z-scheme strain-tunable GeC/ReS$_2$ heterostructure is a promising and efficient photocatalyst for overall water splitting.

items.title: Universal spectrum of weakly coupled quantum critical Ising chains
items.summary: We study the spectrum of arrays of critical transverse field Ising chains perturbed by a weak inter-chain coupling in the scaling limit, using an exact diagonalization algorithm based on Hamiltonian truncation. As the number of chains is made large, we confirm the existence of excitations below the two particle continuum that can be identified with the celebrated Zamalodchikov $E_8$ theory with small corrections. In addition, we find a distinct $ψ$-particle, with mass $M_\mathrmψ$ which is not contained in the $E_8$ theory. Its ratio to the lowest $E_8$ mass ($M_1$) is a universal number, which we have computed numerically to be $M_\mathrmψ/M_1 = 1.819\cdots$ for a one dimensional array of critical chains. We present evidence that this new state fundamentally involves excitations on neighboring chains, explaining why it has no analogue in the single chain problem. Interestingly the $M_\mathrmψ$ mass has a characteristic scaling dependence on detuning from the critical point that is qualitatively distinct from the $E_8$ masses, which can help identify it in spectroscopic experiments on easy-axis magnetic chain materials.

items.title: Constructing physical mechanisms with artificial intelligence
items.summary: Mechanisms recur across the sciences: the equation for heat in a solid also describes molecular diffusion or a Brownian particle. A mechanism is rarely written in one equation; its operation, boundaries, parameters and closures are stated at different steps of a derivation, where methods that read text or fit formulas miss it. We built an equation-native system that reads the equations of all 2.5 million arXiv manuscripts, and show that mechanisms can be compiled from them and constructed by deterministic calculation. A constructor detaches, transfers, unfolds, composes and joins their parts across disciplines; where parts do not fit, the failure is an equation for the missing term. Constructions turn a threshold reactor into a memory that a weak signal writes, an oscillator into a switch through two changes that each fail alone, and a rhythm into the regulator of a chemical amount, each with conditions for an experimental test.

items.title: Adaptive ghost Gutzwiller dynamics of Hubbard model quenches across coupling strengths over extended times
items.summary: Following the real-time dynamics of correlated electrons to extended times, at all interaction strengths, remains an open challenge. We address it with an adaptive time-dependent ghost Gutzwiller approximation (td-gGA). The method extends the Gutzwiller approximation by auxiliary ghost orbitals. It adds more of them whenever the correlations that build up during the dynamics exceed a threshold. This is computationally far more efficient than keeping their number fixed. As a demonstration we take the interaction quench of the half-filled Hubbard model on the Bethe lattice. For this paradigmatic problem, numerically exact nonequilibrium dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) serves as the reference. A previous td-gGA study with a fixed set of 6 ghost orbitals per spin largely reproduced the available DMFT data. It lacked, however, an error estimate that would support predictions beyond them. With up to 16 ghost orbitals per spin, adaptive td-gGA agrees with DMFT wherever DMFT data are available, from the weak-coupling prethermal regime to the strong-coupling collapse-and-revival regime. At strong coupling it remains converged up to three and a half times as long as the DMFT data. Near the crossover between the two regimes, the system relaxes to thermal values that agree with DMFT. Resolving the dynamics in the number of ghost orbitals shows how the sharp dynamical transition of the Gutzwiller approximation turns into this smooth crossover. In the extended time window at strong coupling, we observe that the oscillation frequency is renormalized as predicted by our second-order strong-coupling expansion. With its built-in error estimate, adaptive td-gGA offers a systematically improvable route to the extended-time dynamics of driven and multi-orbital correlated systems, especially when combined with tensor-network or quantum solvers for the embedding problem.

items.title: A Generalized Coherent State Framework for Many-Body Density of States
items.summary: We develop a general framework to calculate the many-body density of states (DOS) of isolated and interacting quantum systems. Based on the generalized coherent state formalism and the Simon-Lieb bounds for a quantum partition function, our method provides a general method of calculation for the DOS in high-dimensional irreducible sectors. This framework further provides rigorous bounds for the ground state energy in each sector and enables the calculation of microcanonical observables across the entire spectrum. Using the Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick (LMG) model as a test bed, we validate our framework by successfully identifying quantum phase transitions (QPTs) and excited-state quantum phase transitions (ESQPTs) across spin sectors. We then study the ferromagnetic transverse field Ising chain with power law interactions, where the hamiltonian ceases to be block diagonal in irreducible sectors. We generalize our coherent states to explicitly track the permutation symmetry group. For the strongly long range interacting case, we demonstrate that the DOS in highest-spin sectors is qualitatively identical to that of LMG-type Hamiltonians in the thermodynamic limit. Unlike existing model-specific numerical or analytical techniques, our formalism relies on general underlying symmetries, making it broadly applicable. It establishes a versatile and computationally efficient bridge between algebraic structure and many-body thermodynamics.

items.title: From Growth Inhibition to Fluctuations: Testing an Ising Model of Bacterial Responses to Antibiotics
items.summary: Complex networks of biochemical reactions have been proposed to exhibit emergent cooperativity that can be described by an effective Ising model, with a small number of parameters encoding collective interactions. Here this mapping is experimentally tested using the response of three bacterial species to a range of antibiotics acting on different cellular targets. The Ising description is compared to the conventional Hill model, examining both the mean growth-rate response and, importantly, its population growth-rate heterogeneity (PGRH). While both models describe the mean growth-rate dependence on antibiotic concentration comparably well, we find that the Ising model provides a markedly better description of PGRH, offering an additional and more stringent test of the collective description. The fitted Ising interaction strength is systematically related to the Hill exponent and increases with the functional distance of the antibiotic target from the protein-production machinery. These results provide experimental support for describing complex biochemical reaction networks through effective cooperative Ising interactions, and suggest that the collective response of bacterial growth to antibiotics reflects the organization of the underlying metabolic network.

items.title: Majorana flat bands from mirror-particle-hole antisymmetry
items.summary: Majorana flat bands, zero modes across the whole edge Brillouin zone, usually rest on chiral symmetry. We show that a fully gapped class-D superconductor can host such a flat band without chiral symmetry or time reversal, provided its superconducting gap is odd under a mirror and translation along the edge is preserved. Combined with particle--hole conjugation, the mirror forms an antiunitary antisymmetry that squares to $+1$ and preserves the momentum along the edge, so it fixes the Kitaev index of every slice of fixed edge momentum. In a gapped bulk, this slice index cannot change with the edge momentum, and the edge zero modes form a band across the whole edge Brillouin zone. We construct a four-band model with exactly these symmetries, a helical $p$-wave superconductor with Rashba coupling in an in-plane exchange field, from which no term can be removed without restoring an additional symmetry. On the mirror lines, its two mirror sectors are exact Kitaev chains. This yields a closed-form phase diagram. Besides the flat band, the model hosts a phase with two Majoranas at each end of a wire, although its class-D index is trivial, and a second-order phase with Majorana corner modes. The spectral localizer detects all these indices in real space, directly on finite-size samples as relevant for experiments. On open rectangular flakes of two widths, it reproduces the phase diagram even though translational symmetry is broken. In the nodal regions, its reading depends on the flake size, so they are left unread. The readings persist under disorder several times the bulk gap. Without translation along the edge, the symmetries protect no more than Majorana parities, and we quantify the signatures that remain specific to the antisymmetry. A minimal model of magnetic adatoms on a triplet superconductor realizes the flat-band and second-order phases.

items.title: Microphase Separation and Ionic Aggregation in Oppositely Charged End-Functionalized Polymer Blends
items.summary: Using an ion-correlation-augmented self-consistent field theory (IC-SCFT), we study the phase behavior of binary blends of A and B polymers carrying single end groups of opposite charge. Under the low dielectric conditions typical for organic polymer melts, strong ion correlations drive association of multiple chain ends, leading to emergent multichain architectures that go beyond a simple ion-paired diblock copolymer picture previously used to interpret recent experiments. At moderate to strong polymer segregation, the resulting phase diagram differs considerably from this effective-diblock prediction: ion clustering broadens the lamellar and cylindrical windows while suppressing the network phases, the reverse of the trend for end-charged diblock copolymers. At weak segregation, the two polymers remain miscible even as ion clustering persists, and decreasing chain length drives the clusters themselves through a sphere-to-cylinder-to-lamella shape transition, connecting continuously to the aggregation behavior of classical terminally charged ionomers in the limit when one of the polymer species shrinks to just the charged end. These results reveal that ion clustering - beyond simple pairwise bonding - shapes the self-assembly of end-charged polymer blends.

items.title: Absence of $σ$-criticality in Short-Range Spin Glasses
items.summary: The stability of ground states in the Edwards-Anderson Ising spin glass in dimensions two and higher against perturbations of a single coupling can be quantified through the ``flexibility'' of that coupling in a particular ground state. The property of $σ$-criticality is one in which varying a single coupling can alter the flexibilities of a (strictly) positive density of couplings in an infinite system, and its presence provides a sufficient condition for the presence of multiple ground state pairs. In a previous paper it was shown for the EA spin glass that $σ$-criticality of the first kind, in which the critical droplet of a bond has a positive-density interface with the ground state, was ruled out in any dimension. The remaining possibility, called $σ$-criticality of the second kind, is one in which a bond lies in the critical droplet boundaries of a positive density of other bonds. We show here that this kind of $σ$-criticality is also absent, ruling out altogether the presence of $σ$-criticality in the EA spin glass. While this doesn't resolve the question of multiplicity of ground state pairs, it removes a sufficient condition for its presence. We then propose a rigorous necessary condition for ground state pair multiplicity.

items.title: Voltage-tunable Josephson diode at zero applied field
items.summary: We report a gate-tunable Josephson diode effect in hybrid nanowire junctions consisting of a spin-orbit-coupled semiconductor core coated with epitaxial ferromagnetic insulator and superconductor shells. The wires display a hysteretic superconducting window as a function of axial magnetic field. In the superconducting regime, the devices exhibit nonreciprocal supercurrent transport, with the diode efficiency showing a strong dependence on back-gate voltage. The effect persists at zero applied magnetic field in a remanent magnetization state following a controlled demagnetization procedure. These findings demonstrate a voltage-controlled Josephson diode in a single junction and suggest a route toward probing intrinsically broken inversion and time-reversal symmetries in hybrid materials.

items.title: Suppression of gel formation by spontaneous fragmentation
items.summary: In this work we study the discrete Smoluchowski equation with a multiplicative kernel and an additional term describing the spontaneous shattering of each particle into monomers at a constant rate $λ$. We show that the introduction of fragmentation suppresses gelation for $λ\ge 4$. We derive analytical expressions for the second moment and the monomer concentration $n_1(t)$. These expressions lead to a recurrence relation allowing the steady-state particle size distribution for $λ\ge 4$ to be calculated with machine precision. We validate our analytical and semi-analytical results via numerical simulations using a solver that employs the Fast Fourier Transform for computation of the right-hand side and a second-order Runge-Kutta method with adaptive time steps.

items.title: Uncertainty-quantified $J$-integral computation for quasicontinuum and finite element methods
items.summary: The $J$-integral is a fundamental concept in fracture mechanics, quantifying the energy release rate that drives crack propagation. This work presents a rigorous implementation and validation of the $J$-integral within the multiscale three-dimensional (3D) quasicontinuum (QC3D) method, along with an uncertainty quantification analysis applicable to both QC3D and conventional FE methods. We compute the 3D $J$-integral under plane-strain assumptions, utilizing continuum mechanics fields (stress and strain energy density) derived from the underlying interatomic potential through the Cauchy--Born rule. Our implementation is comprehensively validated against both linear elastic fracture mechanics (LEFM) theory and the virtual crack extension (VCE) method for three regimes of increasing complexity: small-strain elasticity, and nonlinear deformation without and with atomic relaxation in the region near the crack tip. Excellent agreement is demonstrated in all cases. Further, we introduce a novel Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) framework to statistically assess the uncertainty in $J$-integral results for a given mesh and integration domain in QC3D and conventional FE methods. Our implementation's predictive capability is demonstrated through a QC3D simulation of a three-point bending test on silicon, where the computed critical energy release rate is shown to be in excellent agreement with the Griffith criterion. This work establishes a reliable and efficient framework for evaluating crack driving forces in multiscale fracture simulations with quantified uncertainty, enabling large-scale fracture simulations while resolving atomistic mechanisms at the crack tip.

items.title: Spin Hamiltonian, magnetic anisotropy and excitation spectrum in altermagnetic $α$-MnTe from first principles
items.summary: The hexagonal altermagnet $α$-MnTe combines a near-room-temperature collinear order with a strongly spin-split electronic structure, yet the microscopic origin of its easy-plane anisotropy, its zone-center magnon gap and its anomalously large magnetostriction have remained unexplained. We derive the complete low-energy magnetic Hamiltonian of $α$-MnTe from first principles, combining density functional theory and dynamical mean-field theory with a force-theorem evaluation of the full anisotropic intersite exchange, single-ion terms and classical dipolar couplings. The isotropic exchange, including the altermagnetic splitting of the tenth-neighbor coupling, agrees with inelastic neutron scattering data. Contrary to the common single-ion picture, we find that the easy-plane anisotropy and the magnon gap at $Γ$ are governed by classical dipole-dipole interactions, which enhance the zone-center magnon splitting threefold leading to quantitative agreement with experiment, while the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya term is irrelevant despite its size. The same Hamiltonian reproduces the chiral magnon splitting along antinodal directions, mirroring the electronic spin splitting, and quantitatively accounts for the giant magnetovolume coupling of $α$-MnTe through the volume dependence of superexchange.

items.title: Density-dependent photocarrier recombination in $γ$-InSe
items.summary: We studied the photocarrier dynamics in $γ$-InSe using femtosecond transient reflectance spectroscopy. By measuring the dependence of the differential reflectance on the injected carrier density, we established an empirical relation between the optical response and carrier density, allowing quantitative analysis of the recombination dynamics. The carrier decay exhibits a strong density dependence, indicating a substantial contribution from nonlinear recombination. At high carrier densities, the dynamics are dominated by a second-order recombination process, with a rate constant of $3.8\times10^{-6}~\mathrm{cm^3\,s^{-1}}$. At low densities, the decay becomes approximately exponential, with a carrier lifetime of about 7 ps. We also resolved an initial rise of the band-edge response with a time constant of less than 1 ps, which is attributed to hot-carrier cooling. These results reveal the competition between first-order and second-order recombination in $γ$-InSe and provide quantitative insights into its ultrafast photocarrier dynamics.

items.title: Eigenvalue-based computation of Richardson pairing spectra and finite-size thermodynamics
items.summary: We present a numerical workflow for the reduced BCS Richardson model, combining the eigenvalue-based Bethe equations, Baxter-polynomial reconstruction, and complex root finding. Newton-Raphson iteration solves the nonlinear equations for the eigenvalue-based variables; a linear system yields the polynomial coefficients, and Laguerre iteration with polynomial deflation extracts the rapidities. We apply the procedure to equally spaced, quadratic, and hydrogen-like non-degenerate single-particle spectra as the pairing strength varies. For finite systems, we calculate canonical observables from the complete seniority-zero spectrum and check benchmark spectra against exact diagonalization. In an eight-level, four-pair system with a hydrogen-like spectrum, the heat capacity has two maxima at weak coupling. With increasing coupling, the low-temperature maximum shifts upward and the high-temperature maximum downward; the latter ceases to be a distinct local maximum near $g\simeq0.03515$ in the units used. The equally spaced benchmark instead has a single dominant maximum over the coupling interval displayed for that spectrum. This comparison illustrates how single-particle level spacings can shape finite-size thermal response. The C++ code is publicly available; numerical instabilities remain possible near ill-conditioned configurations and at larger sizes.

items.title: Excess noise and electron-phonon energy transfer in Au wires: Length and temperature effects
items.summary: As a mesoscopic diffusive wire at low temperatures is driven out of equilibrium by a current, excess noise is observed compared to the equilibrium Johnson-Nyquist fluctuations. The expected form of the excess noise varies depending on the relative rates of wire traversal, electron-electron inelastic energy transfer, and electron-phonon inelastic energy transfer. We measure noise as a function of bias current in diffusive Au nanowires on SiO2/Si with lengths ranging from sub-μm to 30 μm and temperatures from 3 K to 50 K, to map out the interplay between charge shot noise and the crossover to electron self-heating and phonon-dominated noise suppression. As expected qualitatively, shot noise is suppressed with increasing wire length and substrate temperature, as electron-phonon scattering is of increasing importance. In long wires, the simple model of electron-phonon energy loss known to be quantitatively effective below a few Kelvin underpredicts the excess noise in the high bias, high temperature limit. This issue is more severe in wires on SiO2/Si than on bare Si, implying that interfacial thermal conduction must be considered in the thermal path even at comparatively high temperatures.

items.title: Electrical Degradation of Vertical $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ Schottky Barrier Diodes Under Au-Ion Irradiation to a Fluence of $1.3 \times 10^7$ cm$^{-2}$
items.summary: The electrical degradation and time-dependent current behavior of vertical $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ Schottky barrier diodes (SBDs) subjected to energetic Au-ion irradiation were systematically investigated. Two successive irradiation exposures were conducted under a constant reverse bias of $-100$ V to evaluate the effects of heavy-ion irradiation on device performance and transient current response. Following irradiation, the devices exhibited degraded forward conduction, increased specific on-resistance, enhanced reverse leakage current, and reduced apparent carrier concentration. During irradiation, pronounced increases in leakage current and transient current spikes were observed. Following each beam termination, the leakage current exhibited an initial rapid decay followed by a slower relaxation process. Single-exponential fitting identified distinct fast and slow relaxation components, while a double-exponential model provided a more comprehensive description of the overall current decay. After the second irradiation exposure, the characteristic time constants of the fast and slow relaxation processes increased from 33.50 to 40.64 s and from 190.35 to 282.29 s, respectively, indicating prolonged recovery dynamics under repeated irradiation. A charge-trapping-based model is proposed to explain the irradiation-induced current enhancement and subsequent fast and slow relaxation processes through modulation and gradual recovery of the effective Schottky tunneling barrier. These findings provide insights into the relationship between heavy-ion-induced electrical degradation and time-dependent current relaxation in $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ SBDs.

items.title: Strong Co-O exchange interaction in $P4/nmm$ KCoO$_2$ and its effect on spin wave and Néel temperature
items.summary: The exchange interactions of a classical Heisenberg Hamiltonian in KCoO$_2$ in the $P4/nnm$ structure are calculated using a linear response approach, derived from the transverse spin susceptibility, integrated over atomic spheres using a projector proportional the local magnetization and including all atoms as magnetic atoms. The exchange interaction between Co and its apical O is found to be by far the largest interaction and ferromagnetic. Its effect on the Néel temperature and the spin wave spectrum are evaluated. The Co-O exchange is found to strongly enhance the critical temperature in the mean field approximation but not in the random phase approximation.

items.title: Translation Method Bounds for 3D Isotropic Conductivity--Shear Modulus and the Search for Attaining Microstructures
items.summary: We compute conductivity--shear-modulus cross-property bounds in three-dimensional isotropic two-phase composites using the translation method, and obtain the tightest bounds reported to date. To assess attainability, we perform unit-cell topology optimization on thousands of distinct initial structures and compare optimized designs to the isotropic bounds using an effective-medium approximation that models the macroscopic material as an isotropic assembly of randomly oriented grains. The best jointly performing designs are consistently bicontinuous, triply periodic minimal surface-like microstructures; however, a small but notable gap to the translation bound remains.

items.title: Imaging Compressible and Incompressible Kinetic Energy of a 2d Bose-Einstein Condensate
items.summary: We introduce a method based on velocity-sensitive two-photon transitions to reconstruct the two-dimensional velocity field as well as the local atomic density of a Bose-Einstein condensate in a single realization. We quantitatively benchmark the method on a quantized vortex. Applied to a condensate far from equilibrium, the method reveals the contrasting behaviors of the system's flow kinetic energy components, where the compressible component quickly decays while the incompressible one remains, dominating the long-time dynamics.

items.title: Categorical classification of non-Fermi liquids in 2+1 dimensions
items.summary: A defining feature of non-Fermi liquids is a lack of the quasiparticle peak on the Fermi surface in the spectral function, which is usually realized by coupling a finite density of fermions with critical collective fluctuations. However, these features of the two- and three-point vertex functions are qualitatively the same across many non-Fermi liquids, which has made it difficult to classify them beyond the definition by negation. We point out that the four-point function in the pairing channel contains rich information that positively differentiates distinct types of non-Fermi liquids. Using the generalized notion of fixed points that captures scale-dependent universal pairing interaction, we provide a non-perturbative classification of 2+1-dimensional non-Fermi liquids. In the large Fermi momentum limit with fixed dimensionless couplings, metals coupled with long-wavelength critical fluctuations are classified into seven superuniversality classes. Each of them exhibits a unique phase diagram in the space of temperature and bare four-fermion coupling. The present work generalizes the earlier perturbative classification to strongly interacting non-Fermi liquids by leveraging kinematic constraints.

items.title: A fermionic framework for quantum machine learning benchmarks
items.summary: We present a framework for building and benchmarking scalable machine learning (ML) models based on simulating free-fermion systems. Our fermionic ML (FermiML) framework is (i) versatile enough to encompass kernel methods and neural networks, (ii) applicable to classification and regression, and (iii) scalable to real-world datasets. FermiML models are quantum circuits sharing the building blocks of most quantum ML (QML) models: (parameterized) qubit rotations and entangling gates. This allows us to build fermionic surrogates that mimic the architecture, and hence the quantum resources and inductive bias, of any QML model while remaining efficiently classically simulable. We thus benchmark QML models against close fermionic counterparts on equal footing and ascertain whether a purported QML gain truly stems from classically inaccessible resources or is an accidental side-effect. Across 31 configurations from five classification datasets, we benchmark quantum kitchen sinks (QKS), instantaneous quantum polynomial (IQP) and generic parameterized quantum circuit (PQC) models against fermionic surrogates. fQKS significantly outperforms QKS and is statistically indistinguishable from IQP and PQC; fPQC outperforms IQP and QKS and ties PQC in 28 configurations. We also introduce fermionic fidelity and Pfaffian covariance kernels for regression and establish QML baselines for this harder task. Finally, we introduce a fermionic energy-based classifier scalable to large text and image datasets, which outperforms prominent QML models on images, beats or closely trails them on text, and stays close to classical baselines throughout. Our results show that while performance depends sensitively on architecture, FermiML yields fermionic surrogates that challenge or outperform their unrestricted counterparts and fermionic QML models that match the scale of classical baselines on real-world datasets.

items.title: High-density correlation energy of the electron gas
items.summary: The high-density expansion of the correlation energy per electron of the unpolarized three-dimensional electron gas, $ε_c = A\ln r_s + B + C r_s\ln r_s + D r_s + \dots$, is used in many approximations to the correlation functional of density-functional theory. The coefficients $A$, $B$ and $C$ are known exactly. We revisit the three diagram classes used to estimate $D$, namely bare rings, rings with one first-order exchange insertion, and third-order diagrams with three distinct momentum transfers. Their sum is $-0.0077880(9)$ Ha per electron, compared with the earlier estimate of $-0.010$ Ha. The difference comes mainly from the coupling-constant weighting of the exchange rings in the calculation of Carr and Maradudin. At order $r_s^2$, seven contributions to the single-logarithm coefficient $E_1$ sum to $(3.653 \pm 0.010)\times 10^{-3}$ Ha per electron. The three long-wavelength contributions to the double-logarithm coefficient $E_2$ sum to $α^2(36π^2 - 208\ln 2 - 221)/(192π^4) \approx -1.433\times 10^{-4}$ Ha per electron, where $α= (4/9π)^{1/3}$. Available diffusion Monte Carlo energies at $r_s = 0.5$ cannot distinguish between the two estimates of $D$.

items.title: Moiré-enabled polariton control in large-angle twisted bilayer graphene
items.summary: Twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) is commonly viewed through two limiting regimes: strongly correlated flat bands near the magic angle and nearly decoupled Dirac cones at large twist angles. Here we explore the intermediate regime. Using hyperbolic plasmon-phonon polaritons (HP$^{3}$) to probe the dynamical electronic response, we investigate bilayer graphene from AB stacking to $5.5^\circ$ TBG. We identify a narrow density window in which the HP$^{3}$ wavelength becomes strongly gate tunable. The window opens when doping suppresses Landau damping and a coherent graphene plasmon emerges. It closes at a second crossover, which appears only above $4^\circ$ and shifts systematically with twist angle. Continuum-model and electrodynamic calculations trace this second crossover to hybridization between the central and remote moiré bands, which weakens the density dependence of the Drude response. The resulting polaritonic tunability is concentrated within a twist-angle-selected density window and produces total wavelength changes approaching $90\%$. Our results demonstrate that remote moiré bands reshape the collective electrodynamics of TBG far from the magic-angle regime and establish large-angle TBG as a platform for gate-reconfigurable mid-infrared polaritons and material cavities.

items.title: Strain-enabled dynamical magnetoelectric coupling in BaFe$_{12}$O$_{19}$
items.summary: Optical excitation has emerged as a powerful tool for manipulating and creating non-equilibrium phases of matter. Yet, the pathways available for optical control are intrinsically limited by the symmetries and interactions of the equilibrium system. Here, we demonstrate that these pathways can be redesigned through atomic-structural engineering to access hidden dynamical properties. By combining resonant vibrational excitation with epitaxial strain, we realize a light-induced, room-temperature multiferroic state in strained thin films of the technologically relevant hexagonal ferrimagnet, barium hexaferrite (BaFe$_{12}$O$_{19}$, BaM). Time-resolved second harmonic generation and magneto-optical Kerr effect measurements reveal an enhanced ferroelectric polarization together with a weakening of the magnetic moment upon exciting mid-infrared phonons in strained BaM thin films, but not in the bulk material. Structural analysis and first-principles-based theory show that this effect is enabled by strain-generated displacement of Fe$^{3+}$ ions, which break the local symmetry and facilitate an emergent dynamical magnetoelectric coupling. Both the strong lattice excitation and strain-induced symmetry breaking are essential for enabling this dynamical coupling, promising an important template for designing otherwise inaccessible non-equilibrium phenomena.

items.title: Ground state and thermal phase diagrams of the magnetized spin-$1/2$ XXZ antiferromagnet on the triangular lattice
items.summary: The spin-1/2 XXZ antiferromagnet on the triangular lattice in a magnetic field is a paradigmatic frustrated quantum magnet, yet its ground-state phase diagram at generic anisotropy and its thermal phase structure remain incompletely understood. Here, using infinite density-matrix renormalization group, infinite projected entangled-pair operator, and exponential tensor renormalization group methods, supported by exact diagonalization, we resolve both issues. At zero temperature, we map the phase diagram continuously from the Ising limit to the Heisenberg point and find that the nonclassical $Ψ$ supersolid is a stable phase just below saturation at all anisotropies studied: it borders the one-third-magnetization up-up-down plateau directly in the strongly easy-axis regime and the semiclassical $V$ phase toward the Heisenberg point. In the strongly easy-axis regime, we uncover an intrinsically finite-temperature bond-nematic phase above the zero-temperature plateau--$Ψ$ boundary, in which the three bond directions become spontaneously inequivalent without transverse spin coherence or three-sublattice order. A hard-core-boson mapping reveals its origin: once thermal fluctuations destroy phase coherence, the field-doped holes settle on domain walls of the local up-up-down order, which are stabilized by quantum kink delocalization and aligned by its $Z_3$ registry. Our results call for reexamining high-field states in triangular-lattice cobaltates such as Na$_2$BaCo(PO$_4$)$_2$ and K$_2$Co(SeO$_3$)$_2$.

items.title: Three-phase contact lines as distinct molecular adsorption environments
items.summary: In wetting and multiphase systems, three-phase contact lines form where liquid, solid, and gas phases meet, creating effectively one-dimensional boundaries with distinct molecular environments. Despite their ubiquity in droplets, liquid menisci, capillary bridges, porous materials, and confined multiphase systems, molecular adsorption at these lower-dimensional boundaries has remained largely unexplored. Here, we use molecular dynamics simulations to show that the contact line on a hydrophobic substrate is not merely the geometric intersection of two interfaces but a distinct thermodynamic adsorption environment with a substantially stronger affinity for amphiphilic molecules than either neighboring interface. The investigated amphiphiles of different molecular structures exhibit a common scaling relation between line and surface adsorption in the dilute regime, while their behavior becomes molecule-specific at higher concentrations. Furthermore, contact-line affinity increases exponentially with alkyl-chain length, leading to crowding at progressively lower concentrations and making contact lines extraordinarily sensitive to trace amphiphilic impurities. Because line, surface, and bulk populations scale differently with system size, contact-line adsorption becomes increasingly important at small length scales, where it can substantially alter molecular partitioning. Contact-line enrichment is predicted to reduce the line tension by an amount comparable to its intrinsic magnitude, with potentially substantial consequences for heterogeneous nucleation. Our results establish molecular adsorption as a fundamental property of three-phase contact lines with implications for wetting and multiphase systems across length scales.

items.title: Origin of quadrupolar order in the 5d$^1$ double perovskite Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$
items.summary: Despite extensive experimental and theoretical studies of quadrupolar order in Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$, the microscopic origin and relative energy scales of the interactions driving it remain unresolved. In particular, the observed ferroic ordering of the $z^2$ quadrupole has remained difficult to explain, as the relative contributions of superexchange, classical quadrupole-quadrupole interactions, vibronic couplings, and virtual excitations to higher-energy levels have not been established quantitatively. Here, we determine all these interactions from first principles and solve the resulting microscopic Hamiltonian. The calculated ground state reproduces the experimentally observed quadrupolar order parameters and the associated structural distortions with quantitative accuracy. Disentangling the individual contributions, we find that ferroic $z^2$ order originates from a linear-quartic coupling, generated by virtual excitations to the $J_{\mathrm{eff}}$= 1/2 doublet and driven by vibronic interactions. Our results establish the hierarchy of microscopic interactions underlying quadrupolar order in Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$ and provide a unified $ab \ initio$ description of its coupled electronic and lattice degrees of freedom.

items.title: Localization in one-dimensional magnetic quasicrystals
items.summary: The celebrated Aubry-André-Harper model undergoes a metal-insulator transition akin to Anderson localization due to an energetic competition between nearest-neighbor hopping and a quasiperiodic on-site potential. In this work, we consider the problem of a one-dimensional lattice subject to a quasiperiodic external field, where the topology of the underlying graph mediates the competition between insulating and conducting phases. In particular, we present examples for which all dispersive eigenstates are critically localized, as well as models in which they are exponentially localized. We also demonstrate the coexistence of these phenomena with an extensive set of degenerate finitely supported eigenstates forming a flat band. Finally, we construct models with exactly solvable mobility edges arising only from graph structure. Going beyond these single-particle results, we show---using exact-diagonalization calculations of the bosonic dynamics---that, as in the conventional Aubry-André-Harper case, on-site interactions drive localized eigenstates toward extendedness. Our results provide a framework for exploring how magnetic interference and interactions jointly constrain transport in quasiperiodic lattices.

items.title: Non-integer high harmonic generation from many-body nonadiabatic gating
items.summary: High harmonic generation (HHG) in solids typically produces a rigid frequency comb locked to exact integer multiples of the drive photon energy. In strongly correlated materials, however, the light field can dynamically transform the electronic state on the timescale of harmonic generation itself, potentially violating this rule. Here, we report giant blueshifted, non-integer HHG in a cuprate Mott insulator Sr$_2$CuO$_3$ produced by mid-infrared excitations. Concurrent transient reflectivity measurements and time-dependent exact-diagonalization simulations of a driven Hubbard model support a many-body temporal gating mechanism that suppresses light emission on the trailing edge of the pulse, thereby blueshifting radiated harmonics in the frequency domain. Our findings establish HHG emission energy as a sensitive probe of quantum many-body dynamics and pave the way for exploration and manipulation of correlated electronic phases of matter with strong-field spectroscopy.

items.title: Tunable first-order transitions and magnetic hysteresis in Bernal pentalayer graphene
items.summary: In two-dimensional electron systems, strong Coulomb interactions can spontaneously lift flavor degeneracies such as spin and valley, producing first-order transitions with hysteretic switching of interest for memory devices. The subband degree of freedom in multiband systems may be viewed as a flavor that not only participates in such transitions but also enables control of the hysteretic behavior, as a displacement field can shift the energy difference between subbands. Here, we demonstrate this principle in Bernal-stacked pentalayer graphene, whose low-energy spectrum comprises a monolayer-like Dirac sub-band together with light and heavy bilayer-like sub-bands. Local compressibility measurements resolve a fully symmetry-broken Landau-level spectrum and a sequence of phase transitions that occur when Landau levels of different subbands cross, at which strong interactions redistribute the occupation among flavors. We show that these transitions exhibit hysteretic Hall responses in magnetic field, confirming their first-order character, and that the magnitude and sign of the hysteresis are tuned by the displacement field, as expected from the subband Landau-level ordering determined in compressibility measurements. Our work establishes the subband degree of freedom in multiband systems as a resource for engineering hysteretic switching, and highlights how local thermodynamic measurements can link microscopic insights to macroscopic responses in quantum materials.

items.title: Tunneling signatures of the Lifshitz transition in a superconducting vortex
items.summary: The Caroli-de Gennes-Matricon states bound to a vortex line in a clean type-II superconductor form one-dimensional minibands that disperse along the vortex. The lowest miniband is separated from the Fermi level by a minigap $E_0\simΔ^2/E_F$. A magnetic field shifts the minibands of the two spin projections in opposite directions. At the threshold field $B^*$ the Zeeman energy equals $E_0$. Estimates for FeSe place $B^*$ at a few tesla. The lowest miniband of one spin projection then crosses the Fermi level, and a spin-polarized one-dimensional Fermi sea forms inside the vortex core. We develop the theory of tunneling spectra across this Lifshitz transition. We solve the Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations numerically in the quantum limit for all momenta along the vortex and compute the local density of states with thermal and instrumental broadening. The zero-bias conductance at the vortex center is absent below $B^*$. It has a maximum near $B^*$ with the inverse-square-root field dependence of a one-dimensional van Hove singularity and decreases at higher fields. The next miniband produces a second onset at a finite distance from the center. The zero-bias signal is carried by one spin projection at the center and by the opposite one in the surrounding ring. We then project the screened electron interaction onto the filled miniband. The resulting Luttinger parameter is close to unity, so the core hosts a weakly interacting one-dimensional Fermi gas. Its quasiparticles relax through three-particle collisions in analogy with thermalization in quantum wires and at quantum Hall edges. The corresponding relaxation rates are established analytically.

items.title: Ground-State Chiral Quantum Clusters
items.summary: Quantum time crystals are states of matter that spontaneously break time translation symmetry, extending the notion of crystalline order to time. While their out-of-equilibrium version has been successfully realized by periodic driving, the equilibrium counterpart remains elusive. Here we introduce "ground-state chiral quantum clusters": self-bound many-body ground states supporting a persistent current. We provide a minimal field theory describing these states, and an exact microscopic realization via the attractive anyonic Lieb-Liniger model on a ring. In the latter, the ground-state density-density correlator exhibits the Talbot effect, with a soliton-like profile that periodically disperses and revives while drifting indefinitely along the ring, realizing persistent motion at equilibrium. Possible experimental probes are discussed.

items.title: Morphogenic necking of surfaces
items.summary: Surface morphogenesis occurs across biological scales, from subcellular vesicles and cells to visceral organs, tissue organoids, and whole organisms. Since morphogenesis often involves changes in topology, a natural question is that of appropriate mathematical descriptions that provide an approach to topological transitions of thin surfaces. Here, we suggest a general intrinsic framework coupling morphogen organization to surface geometry. We propose a minimal geometric model in which smoothing competes with morphogen-induced deformation to regulate shape, while loss of this balance can bring a surface toward a topological transition via neck constriction. A simple dynamical model coupling a scalar field to the surface metric reveals two mechanisms: gradient-driven constriction at steep morphogen transitions and curvature-driven constriction near localized morphogen peaks. For frozen morphogen profiles in simple axisymmetric examples, the gradient-driven route gives exact algebraic contraction, while the curvature-driven route gives local exponential contraction.

items.title: Locality from Nonlocality: Symmetry Relocalization and Gauging of Lattice Dirac Fermions
items.summary: Spatially nonlocal symmetries need not imply nonlocal gauge dynamics. Nonlocal canonical transformations make certain exact nonlocal compact symmetries of free lattice Dirac fermions onsite while retaining sufficient Hamiltonian locality for gauging. Symmetry relocalization yields exact or emergent gauge locality in 1D, 2D, and 3D, subject to lattice structure, topology, and anomalies. In 1D, a Hamiltonian-preserving transformation exchanges onsite vector and nonlocal spectral axial charges of a half-filled chain, enabling local gauging of each and exposing their mixed anomaly. Bosonization identifies momentum-winding T-duality, with a parity-projected operator flowing to a noninvertible topological defect. A nonperturbative norm-resolvent bound proves emergent dynamical gauge locality at finite chemical potential, while a doubled Chern-insulator parent reveals the duality's bulk origin and superconducting extensions reveal hidden compact symmetries. In 2D, the square $π$-flux Majorana model shares the Kitaev honeycomb model's single Dirac fermion and odd Pfaffian parity but supports sharp and exponentially local compact charges, the latter with nontrivial Chern topology. Relocalization retains Schwartz locality for asymptotically local gauging, while AIII/AII parents clarify bulk charge origin and parity-anomaly inflow. Two flavors yield compact $U(2)$, a quaternionic invariant, and asymptotically local non-Abelian gauging. In 3D, an exact mixed vector-axial flux response is derived, while a distinct model supports an exponentially local vector $U(1)$ charge with strong quaternionic topology. A nonlocal map makes the charge and Kramers symmetry onsite while preserving exponential Hamiltonian locality. For a compact $SU(2)$ Weyl doublet, a no-go theorem forbids translation-preserving Gaussian onsite relocalization retaining Weyl content and Hamiltonian locality.

items.title: Surface Nanometal Enables Fast and Hysteresis-Free Optical Hydrogen Detection
authors: Jiamai Ren, Zeliu Li, Xiaotong Li, Yu Guo, Wen Yan, Dawei Li, Fu Zheng, Xinpu Zhang, and Wei Peng
items.summary: Abstract Palladium’s path-dependent hydrogen absorption/desorption and phase-transition kinetics result in hysteresis and nonlinear responses, thereby compromising signal fidelity and repeatability. Herein, we propose and demonstrate a surface nanometal strategy using Au or Pt nanoclusters to regulate hydrogen diffusion. In particular, density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that surface-deposited Pt nanoclusters act as cocatalysts, modulating interfacial electronic structure, accelerating H 2 dissociation, and promoting hydrogen spillover. This increases surface hydrogen chemical potential and eliminates absorption/desorption barrier asymmetry. For the fiber sensor with a 6.8 nm Pd film and 1.84 atomic % Pt loading, a 15 s response time and merely 2.21% maximum hysteresis error are achieved at 3.5% H 2 concentration. Further increasing Pt loading to 4.17 atomic % makes the hysteresis error negligible (only 0.32%), nearly achieving ideal hysteresis-free sensing behavior. Experimental and theoretical results demonstrate that surface nanometal is an efficient strategy for hysteresis suppression while maintaining rapid sensing response.

Using simple examples, we demonstrate that sorting is achieved by resetting the velocity component(s) or orientation of the particles, rather than position. The objects to be sorted are microparticles, modeled as suspended and spatial…

items.title: Molecular regulation and recurrent evolution of fungal bet-hedging conidiation
items.summary: Abstract Bet-hedging (BH) mitigates risk in fluctuating environments by promoting phenotypic diversity within a single genotype. Fungi exhibit remarkable phenotypic plasticity, such as conidiation polymorphism. Here, we show that entomopathogenic Metarhizium species produce either monomorphic or dimorphic conidia, which exhibit marked size variation to support different BH strategies. The large cylindrical and small ovoid conidia produced by the same species possess complementary advantages that facilitate adaptation to different conditions. Large conidia are heavily pigmented, ultraviolet-resistant, and highly virulent, whereas small conidia, produced either on separate phialides or atop large ones, germinate faster and resist bacteria better. These complementary traits represent a classic, yet previously unsuspected, diversified BH strategy. Mechanistic analysis revealed distinct gene expression patterns between morphotypes, leading to the identification of a transcription factor and a lipid-droplet surface protein that play key roles in governing dimorphic conidiation and pigmentation. Phylogenomic reconstruction revealed that later-diverging species reverted to an ancestral, monomorphic medium-spore state, indicating a recurrence of the conservative BH strategy. Pairwise experimental evolution confirmed that monomorphic populations have a fitness advantage under fluctuating ultraviolet irradiation. Our findings establish the BH mechanism in conidiation and reveal evolutionary experimentation with reversion across fungal speciation.

items.title: Nanocatalytic modulation of thrombin-ferroptosis axis for efficient intervention of ischemic stroke
items.summary: Abstract Ischemic stroke represents a leading cause of global mortality. Current therapeutic strategies, including recombinant tissue plasminogen activator and mechanical thrombectomy, are constrained by suboptimal recanalization, high recurrence rates, and reperfusion injury. In this work, we initially identified elevated intrathrombotic thrombin as a critical mediator of fibrinolytic resistance and a driver of ferroptosis-related neuronal injury following stroke. To specifically target this thrombin dysregulation, we designed ultrasmall tungsten-based polyoxometalate (W-POM) nanodots capable of penetrating the blood-brain barrier. In addition to their specific reactive oxygen species-scavenging capability, W-POM nanodots primarily modulate thrombin activity and attenuate its pathological signaling. In both thrombin-induced and ischemia-reperfusion injury models, W-POM nanodots significantly improve neurological outcomes by directly suppressing thrombin activity and inhibiting thrombin-driven ferroptosis. Furthermore, W-POM nanodots remodel the thrombotic microenvironment and reduce neuroinflammation, thereby conferring robust neuroprotection. This study highlights the thrombin-ferroptosis pathway as a key mechanistic axis in stroke and introduces a nanotherapeutic platform for targeted thrombin modulation in ischemic stroke therapy.

items.title: Nucleophile–electrophile chemistry produces a stable interphase for long-Life anode-Less lithium metal batteries
items.summary: Abstract Anode-less lithium (Li) metal batteries (ALLMBs) represent the optimal cell architecture for maximizing energy density, yet their practical viability is severely hindered by poor cycling life. This limitation stems from the unstable solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI), which drives continuous parasitic reactions with Li metal and induces severe interfacial degradation. Here we report a nucleophile–electrophile bridging strategy to construct a robust, passivating SEI that enables long-term stable cycling of ALLMBs. By leveraging a nucleophilic substitution mechanism, electron-rich organic species derived from the solvent, acting as nucleophiles, are covalently bridged by electron-deficient, boron-centred electrophiles derived from the anion. This molecular-level integration overcomes the inherent fragility of the SEI organic phase, generating mechanically robust oligoborates that resist interfacial degradation, along with lithium fluoride (LiF) nanocrystals nucleated in-situ to facilitate rapid Li + transport. The resulting oligoborate–LiF hybrid SEI enables highly reversible Li plating/stripping and remarkably extends the ALLMB cycling life by 12-fold, maintaining 80% capacity over 300 cycles. The superior cyclability is maintained even under stringent practical conditions (high cathode loading, lean electrolyte supply, and pouch-cell operation). This work establishes a fundamentally new paradigm in interphase engineering, paving the way for high-energy, reliable ALLMBs.

items.title: Room temperature giant in-plane anomalous Hall effect in TbMn6Sn6
items.summary: Abstract The anomalous Hall effect is the transverse voltage response in the presence of out-of-plane magnetization or non-zero Berry curvature, which, traditionally, is modulated by an out-of-plane magnetic field. Here we demonstrate a giant in-plane anomalous Hall effect (AHE) induced by coplanar magnetic fields in the quantum magnet TbMn 6 Sn 6 at room temperature. The very large Hall conductivity arises in response to an applied in-plane magnetic field and results from the tilting of the ferrimagnetic axis of the Mn and Tb moments to the out of plane direction. With the in-plane magnetic field aligning the ferrimagnetic axis, the Berry curvature induced giant anomalous Hall effect is observed. Further, we show that the in-plane field induced AHE is more pronounced below the temperature induced spin reorientation, showing a 2π periodicity in angular dependent measurements. Unlike the in-plane Hall effect previously observed primarily at low temperatures, the AHE we observe here represents the largest room-temperature response reported in a single material. Our results reveal strong coupling between an in-plane magnetic field and out-of-plane Berry curvature, enabling new opportunities to engineer spintronic and quantum device responses at practical operating temperatures.

items.title: Solar assisted lithium recovery from brines: challenges and opportunities for integrated system
items.summary: Abstract The rapid projected increases in demand for batteries over the upcoming decades requires a large expansion of lithium production capacity. While hard rock mining currently dominates the worldwide production, brines hold over 60% of global lithium reserves. Lithium production from brines is hampered by low lithium concentrations and high concentrations of other interfering ions such as magnesium. This review comprehensively analyzes integrated solar evaporation methods for capturing the lithium in brines. By firstly reviewing the conventional solar evaporation-chemical precipitation method, a currently commercialized technique, we identify several key challenges, including long timescales, large environmental impacts, and issues capturing lithium in some brine chemistries which prevents it from being applied in more places. A promising strategy to address these challenges is integrating interfacial solar evaporation with adsorption materials. This integration presents several advantages, such as producing both high evaporation and lithium adsorption rates and separating lithium from interfering ions. However, a key issue that needs careful evaluation is scaling taking place on the evaporative surface over time, which can cause significant drops in evaporative flux, thereby lowering the effectiveness of this integrated method. Several anti-scaling technologies have been reported, among which integrated membrane and solar evaporation systems demonstrate excellent potential in maintaining long-term performance of high evaporation and lithium capture rates. Ultimately, integrating interfacial solar evaporation with adsorption/membrane processes has the potential to provide a versatile and sustainable method for capturing lithium from brines with complex compositions.

items.title: Photothermal-driven CO2 hydrogenation to methanol on an integrated Au–MoS2–TiO2 catalyst
items.summary: Abstract Light-driven CO 2 hydrogenation to methanol is constrained by insufficient broadband light utilization and inefficient CO 2 activation. Herein, we achieve highly efficient photothermal hydrogenation of CO 2 to methanol on an integrated Au–MoS 2 –TiO 2 catalyst, in which MoS 2 is anchored on TiO 2 to form an intimate interface, and Au nanoparticles (NPs) are deposited on MoS 2 –TiO 2 . We demonstrate that the MoS 2 –TiO 2 interface induces the formation of few-layered MoS 2 and transfers electrons from TiO 2 to MoS 2 . MoS 2 serves as the primary active phase for CO 2 hydrogenation, while Au NPs enhance photo-to-heat conversion via the localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) effect, thereby collectively facilitating CO 2 activation under mild reaction conditions. Under photothermal conditions at 120°C in a continuous-flow reactor, the catalyst achieves 13.4% CO 2 conversion with 84.7% methanol selectivity, and maintains stable performance over 400 hours without observable deactivation, underscoring it among the most competitive photothermal catalysts for CO 2 hydrogenation to methanol.

authors: Ming-Qiang Fu, Hong-Bin Yao, Zhao-Peng Sun, Ming-jing Bian, Chang-hong Cao, Talgar Shaymurat, Bumaliya Abulimiti and Bei Zhang
items.summary: The ionization asymmetry of hydrogen atom in a synthesized 400–800 nm laser field is investigated by numerically solving the three-dimensional time-dependent Schrödinger equation. The left-right asymmetry of the threshold peak exhibits multiple reversals with the increasing 800 nm laser intensity. The photoelectron momentum distributions show that the addition of 800 nm field leads to increasingly complex interference structures. By analyzing the partial-wave-resolved photoelectron energy spectra and coherent odd–even partial-wave pair contributions, we show that the repeated asymmetry reversals originate from the intensity-dependent redistribution of the contributing partial-wave components and the resulting changes in odd–even partial-wave interference. The accompanying redistribution of the projected excited-state populations is consistent with intensity-dependent changes in the effective multiphoton resonance conditions. The combined population and continuum analyses support a qualitative picture in which varying the 800 nm intensity redistributes the relative contributions of excitation and ionization pathways, thereby reshaping the outgoing partial-wave composition. This partial-wave interference picture provides important insight into multiphoton ionization dynamics and offers a route for coherent control of photoionization asymmetry in atomic and molecular systems.

items.title: Optical Torque Reversal via Electric–Magnetic Spin-Channel Selection
authors: Lv Feng, 侣 冯, Ruohu Zhang, 若虎 张, Zhigang Li, 志刚 李, Bingjue Li, 冰珏 李, Dongdong Lin, 冬冬 林, Binfeng Yun, 斌峰 恽, Guanghao Rui and 光浩 芮
items.summary: Light carrying spin angular momentum (SAM) can exert optical torque and drive particles into rotational motion. Although optical torque reversal has been achieved by tailoring particle properties or incident field parameters, the respective roles of the electric and magnetic components of transverse SAM in governing the torque on an isotropic particle remain unresolved. Here, reversible control of the out-of- plane optical torque on an absorbing isotropic Mie sphere is demonstrated in interference fields formed by two or three plane waves. Two orthogonal linear polarization states selectively activate torque pathways mediated by the electric and magnetic components of the transverse SAM, while intermediate polarization states allow both pathways to coexist. Notably, polarization controls the optical torque by tuning the relative weights of electric and magnetic multipolar contributions. Once higher-order Mie channels become appreciable, competition among these contributions can reverse the total torque and switch the particle rotation between clockwise and counterclockwise directions. These results reveal distinct mechanical roles of the electric and magnetic components of transverse SAM and establish spin-channel selection as a mechanism for polarization-controlled optical torque reversal.

items.title: Hybridization-Induced Enhancement of the Thermoelectric Response in the Kagome Material CsCr6Sb6
authors: Hongye Zhang, Boqin Song, Aifeng Wang, Yisheng Chai, Xiaoyuan Zhou, Ying Zhu, Tianping Ying and Mingquan He
items.summary: Flat bands in kagome lattices provide a prominent route to strongly correlated electronic states. Here we report charge and thermal transport measurements on single crystals of CsCr6Sb6, a kagome Kondo system arising from the hybridization between flat and dispersive bands. The Seebeck coefficient and Nernst signal increase rapidly below TF ~ 70 K, concomitant with the emergence of short-range antiferromagnetic correlations and flat-band resonance. The Nernst coefficient in the intermediate-temperature range of ~30–80 K further follows the universal scaling reported for prototypical heavy-fermion compounds, consistent with the development of strongly renormalized quasiparticles associated with hybridization. Both the Seebeck and Nernst responses reach extrema at a lower temperature Tp ~ 20–25 K, where phonon drag and correlated quasiparticles may both contribute. These results reveal a hybridization-induced enhancement of the thermoelectric response and establish CsCr6Sb6 as a kagome platform for probing flat-band-derived Kondo physics through thermoelectric transport.

items.title: Non-Hermitian skin effect and quasiperiodicity-induced localization in a photonic lattice with staggered on-site potentials
authors: Jia-Yi Li, Zhi-Xu Zhang, Jie Zhang, Kai-Xin Hu, Wen-Xue Cui, Ji Cao and Hong-Fu Wang
items.summary: The quasicrystals combined with nonreciprocal and on-site non-Hermiticity provide a unique platform to explore exceptional phenomena arising from the non-Hermitian skin effect (NHSE). Especially, we investigate a non-Hermitian photonic lattice with nonreciprocal hoppings and staggered complex on-site potentials, revealing an energy-dependent bipolar NHSE and a quasiperiodicity-driven redistribution from skin states to bulk-localized states. Numerical winding numbers and analytical contact conditions reveal the spectral reconnections underlying the bipolar NHSE, with the sign of the imaginary eigenenergy determining its localization direction. Meanwhile, imaginary quasiperiodic modulation drives a crossover from skin localization to bulk localization, while real and imaginary modulations yield comparable bulk localization at strong modulation. Moreover, Fibonacci-size calculations support persistent skin–bulk coexistence, while a separable two-dimensional extension connects one-dimensional localization directions to corner accumulation and spatial redistribution.
