items.title: Thermal-fluctuator-driven decoherence of an oscillator near-resonantly coupled to a two-level system
authors: Thomas J Antolin, Jonas Glatthard and Andrew D Armour
items.summary: Recent experiments on a range of engineered quantum systems have highlighted the important role of interacting two-level systems (TLSs) in modifying device properties and generating fluctuations. Focusing on the case of an oscillator coupled to a single near-resonant TLS, we explore how interactions between the TLS and lower-frequency thermally activated two-level fluctuators (TLFs) degrade the oscillator’s coherence. Depending on the strength of the couplings, a single TLF can give rise to coherence oscillations that appear alongside, or supplant, Rabi oscillations of the oscillator–TLS system. Bath-driven transitions in the TLF cause irreversible coherence decay at a rate that is highly sensitive to both the couplings and the transition rate. For an ensemble of TLFs, we identify and characterise the different regimes of non-exponential phase-averaging-driven coherence decay that the oscillator can display. Using numerical calculations, we examine the extent to which systems with just a few TLFs differ from the limit of a large (continuum) TLF ensemble. Our work provides a theoretical framework for understanding the interplay of coherent TLS interactions and TLF-induced dephasing in quantum devices such as superconducting and phononic resonators.

items.title: Sensitive Thermometry with a Fiber-Integrated Optical Microcavity
authors: Min She, 敏 佘, Qiang Zhang, 强 张, Zhao An, 钊 安, Fan Lv, 帆 吕, Zhaoyi Liu, 兆亿 刘, Jitao Cao, 济韬 曹, Yuhong Zou, 榆红 邹, Ruikai Pan, 瑞恺 潘, Wenpeng Zhou, 文鹏 周, Han Zhang, 涵 张, Jiangshan Tang, 江山 唐, Feng Wang, 峰 王, Franco Nori, Keyu Xia and 可宇 夏
items.summary: High-sensitivity thermometry is critical for cutting-edge technologies such as gravimeters, quantum clocks, and lithography systems. Although recent transformative advances in resonator-based optical microthermometers achieve high sensitivity, the input and output setups are complex and require precise control, severely limiting their practical applications and achievable footprint. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a fiber-integrated thermometer made of a high-Q optical Fabry–Pérot fiber microcavity, filled with transparent but thermal-sensitive ultraviolet glue. The input and transmitted probe laser fields are coupled to the microthermometer via optical fibers, significantly facilitating operation and minimizing the device size. Combining the large temperature dependence of the ultraviolet glue and the micrometer-scale cavity, sensitive thermometry is achieved by independently measuring the resonance shift or the transmission change. Based on evaluation of equivalent temperature noise of the power spectral density, the resonance-shift method achieves microkelvin-level sensitivity. The fixed-wavelength transmission-change method yields a nanokelvin-level readout-referred equivalent temperature-noise floor at high frequencies using quasi-static response calibration. items.summary: Laser cooling of semiconductors requires a high external quantum efficiency for phonon-assisted upconversion while suppressing heat generated by background absorption and non-radiative relaxation. Nanophotonic resonances can strengthen the upconversion channel, but in a single-mode structure may also enhance parasitic pump heating. We introduce a two-cavity non-Hermitian architecture that separates preparation of a lower reservoir state from extraction of the phonon-promoted radiative state. A passive exceptional point, containing no optical gain, is placed in the output branch, where it reshapes the projected final-state optical response; all anti-Hermitian diagonal terms describe radiative leakage, internal absorption, or material decay. For a CdS parameter set, the four-mode calculation gives a 1.23 × 103 enhancement of upconverted photoluminescence relative to a single-mode control, while the pump-induced heat load rises by only 2.8 × 10–3%. The gain consists of a factor of 3.45 × 102 from the independent output resonance and a further factor of 3.56 from exceptional-point tuning.

items.title: An active Lorentz gas: walking droplets in periodic media
authors: Aleksi Majaniemi, Esko Toivonen, Rahil N Valani, Rainer Klages and Esa Räsänen
items.summary: The Lorentz gas is a paradigmatic model in dynamical systems theory for understanding the origin of nonequilibrium transport in terms of microscopic deterministic chaos. In the periodic setting, a point particle scatters elastically off disks arranged on a two-dimensional lattice. Here we replace the disks by smooth potentials and the particle by the widely studied walking droplet, which propels itself on a vertically vibrating fluid. In the low-memory limit, this droplet reduces to a particle with nonlinear active friction. We call this system an active Lorentz gas. Using extensive numerical simulations, we analyse how dissipation generated by the active deterministic dynamics alters the phase-space structure of the corresponding conservative Lorentz gas. We find that islands of stability collapse into attracting and repelling sets. To characterize these structures, we introduce an energy-variance filtering method that distinguishes localized periodic, quasi-ballistic periodic, and chaotic trajectories, enabling the construction of bifurcation diagrams in a non-conservative setting. We identify parameter regimes exhibiting strong bifurcation cascades, anomalous diffusion, and significant phase-space contraction. Our results establish the active Lorentz gas as a rich framework for studying transport in dissipative dynamical systems and provide a bridge between active matter and classical models of chaotic transport, with potential implications for hydrodynamic quantum analogs in periodic media.

items.summary: The decay dynamics of nonlinear nanomechanical systems in phase space via two-tone-drive ringdowns is experimentally explored. Linear and nonlinear libration, scattering off saddles, and metastable states near ghosts with nontrivial energy exchange are observed.

items.summary: Individual atoms trapped in a tweezer array are coupled to a high-cooperativity cavity and coherently excited to Rydberg states, uniting efficient light-matter interfacing with quantum logic operations on a single platform.

items.title: Three-dimensional topological disclination in acoustic crystals
authors: Zhenxiao Zhu, Yan Meng, Minmiao Wang, Xiang Xi, Yuxin Zhong, Linyun Yang, Bei Yan, Jingming Chen, Ziyao Wang, Thomas Christensen, Caigui Jiang, Changqing Xu, Ce Shang, Zhen Gao
items.summary: Topological disclinations are rotational-symmetry-breaking lattice defects that can probe crystalline topology and offer a versatile platform for topological cavities, waveguides, and lasers. Here, Zhu et al. report a three-dimensional topological disclination that carries a fractional charge of 1/2 and hosts zero-dimensional topological bound states embedded in the bulk. The result extends disclination physics beyond layered or surface-based designs and opens new possibilities for controlling waves through the interplay of band topology and defect geometry in three dimensions.

items.title: Spin group symmetry criteria for unconventional magnetism
authors: Xun-Jiang Luo, Jin-Xin Hu, Mengli Hu, Kam Tuen Law
items.summary: Unconventional magnets combine the compensated magnetization of antiferromagnets with ferromagnet-like spin splitting, promising next-generation spintronics, yet a unified symmetry principle for their classification has been lacking. Luo et al. show that just six symmetry operations in the spin space group fully determine the dimensionality and parity of the spin splitting, yielding a complete classification that overturns established paradigms and uncovering numerous candidate materials for even- and odd-parity magnets.

items.title: Conformational dynamics of exopolysaccharides underlie biofilm matrix mechanics in Vibrio cholerae
authors: Kee-Myoung Nam, Nathan Fowler, Rajan Kandel, Yongqi Zhu, Yuchu Liu, Yi-Jhen Lai, Muhammad Faheem Hassan, Emma Gerace, Alexander J. Hinbest, Merrill Asp, Rich Olson, Ying Li, Mu-Ping Nieh, Mingjiang Zhong, Robert J. Woods, Alexis Moreau, Jing Yan
items.summary: Bacterial biofilms are encased within polymeric matrices that allow them to withstand large mechanical perturbations, but how this capability arises from individual matrix components is not well-understood. Combining experiments and simulations, Nam et al. characterize the physical properties of a key polysaccharide in the Vibrio cholerae biofilm matrix and show that it is a semiflexible polymer with unusual nanoscale conformational features that may contribute to its viscosity and, in turn, to biofilm mechanics.

items.title: Combining mass redistribution and momentum redirection for droplet-substrate interaction minimization
authors: Baixue Li, Alexander Oron, Youhua Jiang
items.summary: To minimize droplet-substrate interaction, Li et al. report a reduction in both contact area and time. Pore arrays lead to mass redistribution and momentum redirection of an impacting droplet, where the former facilitates droplet breakup into daughter droplets and the latter promotes droplet liftoff by redirecting the spreading liquids upward.

items.title: Coupled propagation of acoustic topological states
authors: Ming-Zhu Li, Lei Shi, Zhe-Yu Ji, Zhaojiang Chen and Ya-Xi Shen
items.summary: We theoretically and experimentally investigate the coupled propagation of two pseudospin states in an acoustic topological heterostructure. Within the framework of coupled-mode theory, the heterostructure is mapped onto a two-waveguide model, in which the two pseudospin topological states serve as guiding modes. The propagation constants of the individual topological states and the coupling strength between them are quantitatively extracted from the projected band structures of supercells. When the two topological states are decoupled, acoustic energy remains confined to the excited topological interface. When the two topological states are coupled, acoustic energy undergoes Bloch oscillation between two topological interfaces. Notably, the energy-transfer coefficient of the Bloch oscillation can be tuned by introducing interface detuning. Owing to the frequency dispersion of the coupling strength, the heterostructure can function as a wavelength-selective demultiplexer. This work establishes a generalized coupled-mode framework for the quantitative analysis and flexible manipulation of topological-state coupling, offering new insights into the design of topologically protected acoustic devices with controllable multichannel functionalities.

items.title: Optimal learning of quantum channels in diamond distance
items.summary: Nature Physics, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03499-7 Quantum channels can be used to describe the evolution of quantum states, including both unitary evolution and measurement. Now the optimal number of uses needed to learn an unknown channel to any fixed accuracy has been found.
